plain_explanation: A VAE learns to describe an example using a latent distribution and reconstruct it. A GAN learns through a generator and a discriminator. In both cases inspect outputs as well as numerical loss. GAN losses depend on both networks, so a falling value alone does not prove improvement.
worked_example: Supplied VAE reconstruction errors fall from 0.30 to 0.18 to 0.12, while validation error falls to 0.20 then rises to 0.26. This can indicate overfitting. A GAN repeatedly producing the same icon may have poor diversity even when its images look sharp.

exam.question: Label input, encoder, latent sample and decoder in a VAE.
exam.model_answer: Input enters encoder. Encoder predicts a latent distribution. Sample z from that distribution. Decoder reconstructs the input from z.

exam.question: Training error falls but validation error rises. What should you inspect?
exam.model_answer: Inspect held-out examples and overfitting; compare checkpoints and avoid claiming progress from training error alone.

exam.question: A GAN produces only one excellent icon. Is it a successful generator?
exam.model_answer: Not necessarily. Quality may be high but diversity is poor, consistent with mode collapse.
